Narrow Land, Outstretched Imagination - 12 Day Itinerary

Day 1 - Santiago

We landed in Santiago, which served as the launchpad for the rest of the trip.

During the day, we spent our time around Plaza de Armas, checking out the Museum of Fine Arts and La Moneda Palace (home to the Chilean President).

Santiago felt closer to the US or Canada than it’s geographic distance might suggest. Chile was the first South American country to join the OECD and its infrastructure looks the part.

Even the social dynamics resembled the aforementioned North American giants, with more people walking alone and lots of pets! The rest of South America, even the major cities, had more of a communal atmosphere.

Our evening ended rather eerily, with warnings from street-side vendors to go home before it got dark (which we duly heeded).

Day 2 - Rapa Nui

On the next day, we took the long flight to Rapa Nui aka Easter Island. Back in 2023, there was a separate gate for flights to Rapa Nui that’s a bit hard to locate, so be sure to reach the airport early (we almost missed our flight).

Imagine our disbelief when upon landing on the island, we discover our hostel (Hostal Tipanie Moana) is a 7-minute walk, YES WALK, from the airport.

Rapa Nui is as idyllic as you might imagine an isolated island in the South Pacific to be. We spent our day looking for a tour guide for the next day and caught a sighting of our very first Moai (the face-shaped stone sculptures Rapa Nui is famous for) at Ahu Tahai.

A decent restaurant meal cost us about $25, so we quickly discovered the joys of eggs, bread and groceries.

Day 3 - Rapa Nui

This was the day a dream came true.

One of us had been fascinated by the mystical Moai as a child, but never thought they’d see get to see them in the flesh.

With the help of our tour guide, we explored the Ahu Tongariki, the most famous of the statues. The row of Moai staring inland against an empty horizon have an enigmatic air about them that even the best documentaries about Rapa Nui cannot capture.

We learnt the likeliest explanation of how the statues were carved, transported, and raised, but there’s nary an answer for why. The other question about Rapa Nui that’s definitively hard to answer is how the native population almost went extinct.

With these existential thoughts in our head, we spent the rest of the day looking out at the ocean and wondering about the vagaries of human existence.

Day 4 - Rapa Nui

Our last day in Rapa Nui was a buffer day, should the second day have not gone to plan.

The whole point of being in a tropical paradise is to do absolutely nothing and that’s exactly what we did. There’s very little to distract you, making for a meditative morning.

In the afternoon, we caught our flight back to the mainland.

Day 5 - Santiago

Our original plan was a day trip to Valparaiso, but we abandoned the idea after hearing recent safety issues in the area. If things have gotten better (since 2023), then we certainly recommend going as we had also heard great things.

Having explored the hotspots of Santiago earlier, we decided to stroll around the upscale Providencia neighbourhood and catch up with an old friend.

Day 6 - Torres del Paine

Almost week into the trip, we finally head down to Patagonia.

From Santiago, we flew to Puerto Natales, and rented a car to head up to Torres del Paine National Park.

Make sure to fill the tank in Puerto Natales and understand your fuel range. When we visited, there were no petrol stations in or around the park, so we carried an additional 20-litre can.

We set up base in an Airbnb in Cerro Castillo, just outside the park. We were glad they served food (albeit at a slightly steep $22 per meal).

To ease into our adventure, we started with the viewpoints around Laguna Amarga and the Paine river.

Day 7 - Torres del Paine

We drove to Lago (lake) Grey and walked to Glaciar (glacier) Grey viewpoint. Somewhere along the way, we caught sight of the legendary Las Torres, the iconic granite trio of towers, that we were set to climb to the base of tomorrow.

We were supposed to drive over to another viewpoint, but instead, spent a few hours helping out a family of tourists whose car broke down. Golden rule and all that. No regrets though, as we ended up having a wonderful dinner with them after their vehicle was fixed.

Driving at night is a bit scary because of rabbits that pop out of nowhere!

Day 8 - Torres del Paine

Sigh. The hopes we had for this day.

The hike to the base of Las Torres was supposed to be the highlight our Patagonian adventure. And it was, until it wasn’t.

We were a little late to get going from our Airbnb and only began the hike around 10:30 AM. We rapidly made our way to the final leg (only stopping briefly to take in breathtaking views), but were stopped by the park rangers who refused entry. Apparently, you must reach this point by 2:00 PM, and we made it by 2:15 PM.

To compound our misery, the rangers were extremely rude to us.

Day 9 - Torres del Paine

Thankfully, the park redeemed itself under clear skies the next day.

Our search for azul (blue) took us to Lago Nordenskjold, Salto Grande, and the Cuernos and Condor viewpoints. The red mists of the day prior were replaced by turquoise lakes and white capped mountains.

This was Patagonia exactly as advertised, and made for the fond memories that we thought we might not have.

Day 10 - Punta Arenas

We took the 3-hour bus down to Punta Arenas, the southernmost town in the world with over 100,000 inhabitants.

In our excursion around the edge of civilization, we discovered a Hindu temple, which had to be the southernmost of its kind.

Day 11 - Punta Arenas

Take a wildlife excursion to Isla Magdalena and Isla Marta.

We walked among penguins, watched sea lions and heard birds everywhere. It is difficult to maintain adult composure around a field of penguins, and we did not try.

Punta Arenas also has a Hindu temple, which was sadly closed when we went and may be among the southernmost temples of its kind anywhere. It turns out Indian merchants from the Sindhi community had established a community over a century ago! Incredible where trade takes people.

Day 12 - Santiago

We returned to Santiago and had a half a day to kill before our flight out the next morning. We decided to visit the Sky Costanera observation deck, but no city’s panoramic views could compare to the mountains of Patagonia.
